history.content: 2 facts about the great wall of china

1) The Great Wall of China is a series of fortifications made of various materials, such as stone, brick, tamped earth, and wood, which were built along the historical northern borders of China to protect the Chinese states and empires from invasions and raids by nomadic groups. 2) The majority of the existing wall dates back to the Ming Dynasty (1368-1644).
who and when the great wall of china start to be built?

The initial construction of the Great Wall of China started when fortifications built by various states during the Spring and Autumn (771-476 BC) and Warring States periods (475-221 BC) were connected by the first emperor of China, Qin Shi Huang, to protect his newly founded Qin dynasty (221-206 BC) against incursions by nomads from Inner Asia. Records show that in the Kaiyuan era, the general Zhang Yue built a wall 90 li although it remains unclear. In 214 BC, Qin Shi Huang ordered new fortifications to be built on the great wall of China.
does the great wall of china have special meaning in its chinese name?

Yes, the Chinese name of the Great Wall, "Chángchéng" (长城), literally translates to "The Long Wall". The alternative Chinese name, "Wànlǐ Chángchéng" (万里长城) or (萬里 長城), means "The 10,000-li Long Wall", with "li" being a traditional Chinese unit of distance, and this name is figurative, representing the idea of an innumerable or immeasurable distance. The Chinese character 城 is a phono - semantic compound of the place '' or earth '' radical 土 and 成.
did "the great wall of china" always had name as "the great wall of china" in english?

No, the Great Wall of China has historically had a number of different names in both Chinese and English. the current English name "The Great Wall of China" evolved from accounts of "the Chinese wall" from early modern European travelers. By the 19th century, "The Great Wall of China" had become standard in English, French, and German, although other European languages continued to refer to it as "the Chinese wall."
it is so interesting to know that people are already able to build a wall from long long long time ago

Yes, it is indeed fascinating. The Chinese were already familiar with wall-building techniques during the Spring and Autumn period between the 8th and 5th centuries BC. During this time and the subsequent Warring States period, several states constructed extensive fortifications using materials like earth and gravel.
I heard of a myth about the great wall of china. Do you also think we can see the wall from the moon since it is really long and big?

No, the Great Wall of China is not visible from the moon. This is a common myth, but the wall is only 9.1 m (29 ft 10 in) wide and its color is similar to the surrounding soil. The optics of resolving power make it impossible for the unaided eye to see an object as thin as the Great Wall from the moon, which is about 384,393 km (238,851 mi) away from Earth. This misconception might have originated from a letter written in 1754 by William Stukeley and was further popularized in the late 19th century due to the discussion about "canals" on Mars.

The Berlin Wall ( German : Berliner Mauer , pronounced ( bɛʁˈliːnɐ ˈmaʊ̯ɐ ) ( listen ) ) was a guarded concrete barrier that physically and ideologically divided Berlin from 1961 to 1989 . Constructed by the German Democratic Republic ( GDR , East Germany ) , starting on 13 August 1961 , the Wall cut off ( by land ) West Berlin from virtually all of surrounding East Germany and East Berlin until government officials opened it in November 1989 . Its demolition officially began on 13 June 1990 and finished in 1992 . The barrier included guard towers placed along large concrete walls , accompanied by a wide area ( later known as the `` death strip '' ) that contained anti-vehicle trenches , `` fakir beds '' and other defenses . The Eastern Bloc portrayed the Wall as protecting its population from fascist elements conspiring to prevent the `` will of the people '' in building a socialist state in East Germany . In practice , the Wall served to prevent the massive emigration and defection

Janet Davies proposed that the origins of Welsh language were much less definite ; in The Welsh Language : A History , she proposes that Welsh may have been around even earlier than 600 AD . This is evidenced by the dropping of final syllables from Brittonic : * bardos `` poet '' became bardd , and * abona `` river '' became afon .
